title: Separate historical reviews from recheckable audit candidates
body: Expanding documentation discovery and demoting speculative path/module findings exposed a repair lifecycle trap: treating every candidate like a historical advisory left ordinary completed renames permanently incomplete. Missing-path, missing-script, and unmentioned-directory candidates can carry resolution: recheck; the original evidence is retained, and rerunning the same check can establish that its condition is no longer detected. That is not semantic approval. Dependency-history and decision advisories require a separate assessment even after documentation changes or commits. Keep unavailable inputs and deleted/empty original documents unverified. The audit-scope and automation regressions cover candidate resolution through the final commit while historical advisories remain review-required. This is an implementation lesson, not an independently accepted policy.

sources.note: Recheckable missing-path candidate resolves while a historical dependency advisory stays open.
Rename verification across both host lifecycles and the final documentation commit.
